# Calibrating bounded-width innovations for a reusable fast-source model

31 October 2026. Author construction, pending independent review. This is a receiving theorem for a known mechanism with an unknown innovation law, not identification of an unrestricted hidden process. The estimator and its concentration inequality are ordinary finite-alphabet statistics. The additional consumer is the separately reviewed complete-CQ perturbation bound.

## 1. Known mechanism and unknown parameter

The fully observed state is x in GF(2)^n. At each clock event it updates by

    y = F x + G r + beta,

with known binary F, G, beta. F is invertible, G has k independent columns, 1<=k<=n, and the controllability matrix [G,FG,...,F^(n-1)G] has rank n. Innovation words r in GF(2)^k have an unknown, fixed law p, are independent across events, and are independent of prior source/system states and interventions. The clock rate lambda is known separately. These are structural promises, not statistical conclusions from a finite transcript.

The known reference P0 uses u(r)=2^-k; the actual kernel Pp uses p. Let m be any acquired controllability horizon for which [G,...,F^(m-1)G] has rank n; m=n always suffices. Binary elimination computes such a horizon in polynomial n time. Denote by pi the uniform law on all n-bit states and by Pi=pi 1^T its reset matrix.

For every fixed r, x -> F x+G r+beta is a permutation. Consequently Pp pi=pi for EVERY p, without estimating p or a stationary distribution. Also

    x_m = F^m x_0 + sum_(j=0)^(m-1) F^j beta
                    + sum_(j=0)^(m-1) F^j G r_(m-1-j).

Under u the last sum is uniform on the image of the controllability matrix, hence uniform on GF(2)^n. Thus P0^m=Pi.

For any fixed x, injectivity of G makes r -> F x+G r+beta one-to-one. Therefore the column difference is exactly

    sum_y |Pp(y|x)-P0(y|x)| = sum_r |p(r)-u(r)|,
    eta := ||Pp-P0||_1 = ||p-u||_1.

This equality does not require enumerating 2^n source states. It fails as stated for a noninjective G; this receiver requires an acquired basis of the actual innovation coordinates rather than silently identifying redundant coin laws.

For each fixed x, full-column-rank G makes the innovation-to-output map injective. Therefore the absolute column-sum difference equals ||p-u||_1, identically for every x, and the full induced matrix norm is exactly this quantity. This eliminates a 2^n transition-table estimation problem only because the mechanism and innovation coordinates are known. # Executable calibration scope and conservative costs

31 October 2026. The mathematical receiver and this executable are separate review targets.

`calibrate_affine_innovations.py` exposes `calibrate(F,G,beta,transitions,*,N,radius,delta,b,T,p_slots,epsilon_model)`. Matrices are lists of integer bits; integer source labels use the low bit as coordinate zero. Budgets accept integers, rational strings or `Fraction`, never binary floating point.

The executable validates the stated mechanism's algebraic prerequisites, computes the classical controllability horizon, checks each residual is in im(G), and returns PASS/ABORT using exact rational arithmetic. It uses the deliberately conservative confidence certificate

    N radius^2 >= 2(2^k+j),       2^-j <= delta,

with the smallest such integer j. Indeed 2^D exp(-N radius^2/2) <= 2^(D-floor(N radius^2/2)) <= 2^-j. This avoids floating logarithms entirely. A sparse histogram includes all absent symbols' contribution analytically.

Exactly N pairs must be supplied. The caller must commit N and budgets before observing data and must supply all actual clock events if using trajectory pairs. The code cannot establish those historical facts, detect an N-pair change-only record presented as complete, verify fresh iid innovations, establish the known mechanism from finite data, verify the supplied Hamiltonian bound b, or acquire the clock rate. It cannot prevent a user from repeatedly running the test until PASS; such selection needs a separately allocated confidence budget. The `model_promise_verified` output is always false.

A passing record can be rare and misleading. The tests deliberately retain a balanced transcript which passes under the assumed confidence protocol but has positive probability under a true innovation law (9/10,1/10), whose actual distance4/5 exceeds the test threshold1/4. This is statistically permitted, not an implementation defect. Confidence is an unconditional false-PASS bound under the declared protocol, not per-transcript truth or conditional-on-PASS certainty.

`test_affine_calibration.py` tests exact PASS/ABORT threshold arithmetic, fixed sample-count boundaries, malformed algebraic mechanisms, failed controllability, off-image transitions, invalid labels/budgets, all-tick self-loop extraction, and exhaustive recovery for all injective n-by-k matrices with1<=k<=n<=3.
